sections.title: The Meeting
sections.content:
Project MAC will host a Network Graphics Meeting on the 18th, 19th and 20th of July 1971 at the MIT Endicott House, 20 Haven Street, Dedham, Massachusetts. A map and written directions from Boston's Logan airport and from MIT are attached to the original.

Attendees should arrive between 4:30 and 6:00 p.m. on Sunday, July 18th. The meeting formally starts at 6:00 p.m. that day and ends after lunch on Tuesday, July 20th. Attendees are invited to visit Project MAC for open discussions or demonstrations afterwards.
sections.plainLanguage: It is a short camp for people who work on computer pictures. You show up on Sunday evening and go home after lunch on Tuesday.

sections.title: Ground Rules for Attendance
sections.content:
The ground rules and discussion topics are those outlined in RFC 87. Each organization represented is expected to present one or more working papers in one or more of the chosen areas. A minimal working paper is a set of written notes plus an oral presentation.

The author suggests that the RFC mechanism be used to distribute the written notes. Authors who do not use it must mail a copy of their notes to each attendee by July 1, 1971.
sections.plainLanguage: To come, every group must bring something to share: a few written pages and a short talk.

sections.title: Deadlines and Reservations
sections.content:
Reservations are made by contacting the named Project MAC staff by telephone or by mail, and all attendees are asked to reserve by June 1st. RFCs and working notes that relate to the meeting should reach the organizer by Tuesday, June 22nd.

A bibliography of reading material and a list of prospective attendees will be published by June 25th. Each presenter can expect a telephone call about July 5 to find how much time is wanted, and the times will be scaled to fit the schedule.
sections.plainLanguage: There is a sign-up date, a date to hand in your papers, and a phone call to decide how long each person gets to talk.
